fair_value_reason: NTM EPS at Oct-2027 of about $48 (the agents' case weights, with the 'flat price per EB' case corrected for guided exabyte growth from ~$40 to ~$45) x 16.5x = $792, plus about $15 per share of cash build net of buybacks = $807 (weight 0.6). FCF of about $41 per share (0.86 conversion) at a 5% yield = $826, + $15 = $841 (weight 0.4). Blend is about $820, vs the round-2 mean of $794, my round-1 $805 and the $837.52 close. It is about 2% below spot, which is within the error of the multiple assumption.

thesis_triggers.event: About $520 (-38%) is roughly 11x reconciled NTM EPS of about $48, near the HDD peak-cycle multiple. Below it the market would be pricing an actual break in CY2028 contract pricing (price per EB falling in new LTAs, hyperscaler BTO deferrals, a Mozaic 4/5 slip), not 70%-vol noise; 2026 one-day sector shocks bottomed around $700-760. Same as the forecasters' mean.

supervisor_summary: STX closed at $837.52 after an 11% drop on the Toshiba capacity report. Round 2 narrowed the forecasters' fair values to $770-815 (mean $794), but mostly by anchoring on my round-1 framework rather than through new independent evidence. My checks verified agent 5's Kalshi 22% (with volume in contracts, not dollars), found agent 4's new tracker data real but too weak to move the forecast, and confirmed agent 1's correction that the September one-off pricing effect was minor. The one substantive change is arithmetic: the agents' 'flat CY2028 pricing' cases drop the guided mid-20s exabyte growth and understate the cash build. That lifts my fair value to about $820 (about 2% below spot) and the middle of the ladder by about a point. The multiple paid for peak earnings and CY2028 contract pricing remain unresolved, so confidence is low. With about 70% volatility there is no clear Sharpe edge over the S&P 500.
key_drivers: CY2028 nearline contract pricing: volume is allocated into CY2028, but prices are set only through CY2027 (Q4 FY26 call), so the Toshiba/WDC supply response acts on the 2028 negotiations, which are likely largely set by the April-July 2027 reports.

Whether mid-20s exabyte growth holds into 2028: with growing exabytes, even flat price per EB lifts NTM EPS to about $45-46. Only falling price per EB or stalled demand produces the $38-41 the agents use as 'flat'.
The multiple the market pays in Oct-2027 for likely peak earnings (16-18x assumed vs 8-15x HDD history): this is the largest unresolved judgment.
Toshiba's effective exabyte add (~¥60B doubling by March 2028, MAMR-only until FY2028 HAMR, outside heads/media): probably +3-6% to industry exabytes by end-2027.
The Q1 FY27 print and Q2 guide in late October, and the capital-return mix (buybacks vs cash build) that sets net cash per share.
